create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT-based machine-to-machine authentication creates service accounts derived from the provider name and JWT subject, rather than logging in as a pre-existing human user.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity returned after login_with_jwt may be a generated service account name, so differences from the raw JWT sub are not automatically an identity-collision bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Externally issued JWT authentication is documented as signature+expiry validation against configured sources; no jti replay tracking is documented.
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same valid external JWT may succeed by design for stateless verification and should not be flagged as replay unless a stronger one-time guarantee was explicitly configured elsewhere.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive a refresh token when offline_access is requested and configured; otherwise only an access token is returned.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing refresh_token is expected unless offline_access is enabled on both sides.

oidc_jwt.description: If a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested, excluding special scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: A token containing broad claims after an empty-scope request is expected behavior, not scope escalation.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive refresh tokens when offline_access is both configured and requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing refresh_token without offline_access is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: A token can only be introspected from the same provider used to authenticate, unless it is first exchanged for a token from that provider.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-provider introspection denial is expected and should not be treated as an authorization bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive an access token by default; refresh tokens are only returned when offline_access is requested and configured.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider docs - Authorization code / Refresh token grant
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of refresh_token is expected and should not be treated as a token issuance bug.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT in the same setup. Documentation only guarantees that externally issued JWTs are checked for valid signature by selected federated OIDC sources and that exp is not now-or-past; without a valid control, a failed attack login could be caused by bad provider/source wiring rather than freshness enforcement.

For I1 trust-anchor and resigning tests, configure_jwt_validation must select the exact Federated OIDC Source(s) or Federated OIDC Provider(s) whose JWKS/authentik-issued tokens should be trusted. login_with_jwt accepts any JWT signed by any selected source/provider; if multiple trust anchors remain selected, attacker-signed tokens may be accepted by design.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, authentik does not document a built-in issuer binding parameter for JWT M2M authentication. The docs explicitly recommend using an Expression policy over request.context['oauth_jwt'] to enforce claims such as iss. Therefore, the fuzzer MUST add a policy check on oauth_jwt['iss'] when testing issuer enforcement; otherwise acceptance of a wrong issuer is expected configuration, not proof of a verifier bug.

For I5 audience-binding tests on login_with_jwt, authentik documentation does not state that input JWT aud is validated for externally issued JWT authentication. The documented built-in checks are signature trust and exp freshness. Therefore, the fuzzer MUST enforce aud via an Expression policy over request.context['oauth_jwt'] or treat missing audience enforcement as unconfigured behavior rather than a vulnerability.

For I5 claim-binding tests on login_with_jwt, authentik exposes parsed JWT claims to policies as request.context['oauth_jwt']. There is no documented bound_claims or bound_subject parameter with wildcard or exact-match semantics for this flow. The fuzzer MUST implement claim restrictions through Expression policies and MUST NOT assume Vault-style exact/glob matching knobs exist.

For I5 numeric claim coercion tests, authentik documentation does not specify cross-type comparison semantics for Expression policy evaluation over request.context['oauth_jwt']. The fuzzer SHOULD explicitly test integer-vs-float comparisons in policy expressions, because acceptance or rejection depends on Python expression logic rather than a documented claim-matching mode.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, JWKS data from an OAuth Source is fetched when the source is saved and 'No automatic re-fetching is done.' Therefore, rotating keys at the upstream JWKS endpoint alone is insufficient. The fuzzer MUST update/save the source or otherwise refresh the configured JWKS in authentik before expecting old keys to be rejected.

For I3 config-change sequences involving source/provider updates, authentik documents that changes to associated app/provider configuration immediately trigger outpost updates via websockets, but OAuth Source discovery/JWKS fetching is performed on save and not automatically re-fetched later. A valid coherence test must compare behavior before and after an explicit config update/save, not after only changing the remote discovery/JWKS document.

For OIDC authorization-code flow tests, redirect_uri validation can use exact values or administrator-supplied regular expressions. The fuzzer MUST distinguish exact redirect URI matching from regex-based acceptance. If regex is configured, broader matches may be by design and are not evidence of redirect_uri_mismatch unless the accepted URI falls outside the configured regex.

For OIDC request-object alg_none tests, start_oidc_auth may include a 'request' JWT parameter, but the provided documentation does not describe request-object signature validation settings or supported request object algorithms. The fuzzer SHOULD treat any result as implementation-specific unless discovery or provider configuration explicitly documents request object signing requirements.

For OIDC RP validation tests generally, the documentation states authentik follows the OIDC spec and the glossary for ID tokens states RPs validate issuer, audience, signature, expiry, and nonce. When authentik is acting as an RP via OAuth Sources, the fuzzer should expect nonce/aud/iss/exp validation to matter, but only where the source/provider is configured as an OIDC source rather than JWT M2M authentication.

For token introspection tests, documentation states you are only able to introspect a token from the same provider that was used to authenticate, or you must first exchange the token for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspect_token with the matching provider credentials; cross-provider introspection failures are expected and not an authorization bug.

For I5 scope-escalation tests, when a client requests no scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested, except special scopes. The fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope string in baseline and attack requests; omitting scope broadens claims by design and will create false positives.

For refresh-token or offline-access related tests, starting with authentik 2024.2 applications only receive a refresh token when both the application/provider is configured with the offline_access scope mapping and the request includes offline_access. The fuzzer MUST configure and request offline_access explicitly; absence of refresh_token is otherwise by design.

The token endpoint at /application/o/token/ requires application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests for OAuth2 grants. Do NOT send JSON bodies for login_with_jwt, exchange_code_for_token, token refresh, or device-code polling.

For I2 expired_token tests against login_with_jwt, authentik explicitly checks that the input JWT exp claim is not now or in the past. Use a control token with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and an attack token with exp={{now_epoch_minus_60}} so LOGIN_FAILED can be attributed to expiry enforcement rather than broken setup.

For I2 replay_same_token on oidc_jwt M2M login, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same externally issued JWT as a vulnerability by itself. The documentation only states signature and exp validation for external JWTs and does not describe jti tracking or one-time-use semantics for these bearer JWTs.

For I1 resign_attacker_key and kid_injection tests, configure the target OAuth2 provider to trust only the intended Federated OIDC Source(s) or Federated OIDC Provider(s). authentik accepts any JWT signed by any selected source/provider certificate, so a test is invalid if attacker-controlled keys are accidentally included in the configured trust set.

For I1 trust_anchor_substitution tests with external JWTs, the documentation only guarantees signature verification against selected source certificates and exp validation. Issuer validation is not automatic; if issuer restriction is desired, it must be enforced with an Expression policy using request.context['oauth_jwt']['iss']. Do NOT report missing issuer enforcement unless such a policy was configured.

For I5 audience and scope tests on oidc_jwt M2M login, remember that access can be dynamically limited by Expression policies using request.context['oauth_jwt'] and request.context['oauth_scopes']. A valid authorization-binding test must control provider policies; otherwise a denial may come from policy logic rather than built-in JWT validation.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, if the provider is configured with a JWKS URL on an OAuth Source, authentik fetches the discovery/JWKS data upon saving the source and does no automatic re-fetching. To test rotation coherently, the fuzzer MUST perform an explicit reconfiguration/save step after changing upstream keys; otherwise continued acceptance of the old key may reflect stale cached trust material by design.

For I3 config-change sequences involving OAuth Source discovery, NEW logins after saving the source use the newly fetched discovery/JWKS metadata by design. A valid coherence test must compare behavior before and after an explicit save/update, not assume background refresh.

For OIDC authorization-code flow tests, redirect_uri validation is enforced against the provider's configured Redirect URI list, and regex values are supported. When testing redirect_uri_mismatch, use a redirect_uri that is outside the configured exact value or regex; otherwise acceptance may be by design.

Redirect URI matching supports exact URLs and administrator-configured regular expressions. For security tests, do NOT assume wildcard semantics unless the provider was explicitly configured with a regex. A plain redirect URI value is exact-match oriented; regex behavior only exists when the admin intentionally uses a regex pattern.

For I5 empty_audience and audience_mismatch style tests in oidc_jwt M2M mode, the documentation does not describe a built-in bound_audiences-style constraint on input JWTs. Audience-like restrictions must be implemented through provider/source selection or Expression policies over request.context['oauth_jwt']. Do NOT report missing audience enforcement unless such policy/configuration was actually set.

For I4 cross_user_collision tests on oidc_jwt M2M login, authentik creates service accounts based on the provider name and the subject claim of the input token. Different providers can therefore intentionally namespace identities separately. Cross-provider identity differences are not evidence of a collision bug.

For I4 cross_mount_collision or cross_provider_jwt_audience scenarios, test the SAME target provider/client_id unless the goal is explicitly cross-provider isolation. The service account naming scheme includes the provider name, so identities from different providers are expected to differ by design.

For I2 freshness tests on authorization codes, authentik documents that authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly. Reuse of the same code should be tested at the token endpoint, not by comparing identities. Assert rejection via non-200 HTTP status on the second exchange.

For refresh-token related tests, starting with authentik 2024.2 the refresh token grant requires the offline_access scope, and applications only receive a refresh token when both the application and authentik are configured for offline_access. Do NOT treat absence of refresh_token as a bug unless offline_access was requested and configured.

When no scopes are requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested, except special scopes. For I5 least-privilege tests, always send an explicit minimal scope set; omitting scope broadens claims by design and can create false positives.
For verify_granted_identity, use the access_token as the Bearer credential. The id_token is an identity assertion and is not the API credential for /application/o/userinfo/.

For introspection tests, authentik requires authentication to the introspection endpoint, and you may only introspect a token from the same provider used to authenticate unless you first exchange it for a token from that provider. Cross-provider introspection failures are expected by design.

For I5 token_exchange and cross-provider token reuse style tests, the provided oidc_jwt documentation only documents /application/o/token/ for standard grants and JWT-based client_credentials, plus a separate introspection restriction that tokens are provider-scoped. Do NOT infer RFC 8693 token exchange support from these docs.

For OIDC RP validation tests against authentik as a relying party via OAuth Sources, discovery metadata is fetched on save and replaces configured URLs, but no automatic re-fetching is done. If testing issuer/JWKS changes upstream, the source must be re-saved before expecting new validation behavior.

For I2 token-freshness tests against login_with_jwt, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT alongside the attack JWT. authentik documents that externally issued JWTs are accepted only if signed by a configured Federated OIDC Source and if exp is not now or in the past; authentik-issued JWTs must also not be revoked. Without a control, a failed login may reflect bad provider/source setup rather than exp/nbf enforcement.

replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti are BY DESIGN for externally issued JWT authentication unless you are testing authentik-issued access tokens that can be revoked. The documentation only requires signature validation and exp checking for external JWTs; it does not document jti tracking or one-time-use semantics. Do NOT flag acceptance of the same external JWT twice as an I2 vulnerability.

For I1 trust-anchor and key-substitution tests on login_with_jwt, configure the OAuth2 provider to use the intended Federated OIDC Source(s) or Federated OIDC Provider(s) first. authentik accepts any JWT signed by any selected source/provider certificates. If multiple trusted sources/providers are selected, a token signed by any of them is expected to authenticate.

For I1 expired-token tests on external JWT login, set exp to {{now_epoch_minus_N}} for the attack token and exp to {{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for the control token. authentik explicitly checks that external JWT exp is not set as now or in the past.

For I5 audience/scope tests on the OAuth2 provider, do NOT omit scope and expect least privilege. When a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. This can make overbroad claims appear by design. Always request the minimal explicit scope set needed for the test.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider docs - Default & special scopes

oidc_jwt.constraint: For refresh-token or offline-access scenarios, request offline_access explicitly and ensure the provider is configured with the offline_access scope mapping. Starting with authentik 2024.2, applications only receive an access token by default; refresh tokens require offline_access on both sides. Do not treat missing refresh_token as a security failure without this setup.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider docs - Authorization code / Refresh token grant

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, authentik validates redirect URIs against the provider configuration. The docs state redirect URIs are validated and may be configured as exact values or regexes. If the provider uses a regex redirect URI, multiple callback URLs may be accepted by design. Build the oracle against the configured regex, not exact-string assumptions.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider docs - Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Redirect URI matching supports regex when configured by the administrator; it is not exact-only in all deployments. For redirect_uri mismatch tests, first determine whether the provider uses a literal redirect URI or a regex. A callback accepted by a configured regex is BY DESIGN and not an I3 failure.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider docs - Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For OIDC request object tests (oidc_request_object_alg_none), send the JWT in the request query parameter to /application/o/authorize/. The docs explicitly mention the optional request JWT on the authorization endpoint. Because the documentation does not state request-object signature policy knobs, treat this as a direct authorization-endpoint behavior test and assert on HTTP/redirect outcome rather than assuming a configurable enforcement setting exists.
oidc_jwt.source: Task-required standard OIDC endpoint extraction plus authorization endpoint docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 authorization-code replay/coherence tests, use the same code twice at /application/o/token/ and assert the second exchange fails. authentik documents that the authorization code can only be used once and expires quickly. This is the correct oracle for code replay, state swap, and code injection style tests.

For PKCE-related tests, send token requests as application/x-www-form-urlencoded to /application/o/token/ and include code_verifier only when the scenario requires it. Assert on non-200 HTTP status for rejection cases rather than comparing identities. This avoids false positives from flow-level redirects or consent behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: Token endpoint glossary and OAuth2 token endpoint examples

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 scope-escalation tests using UserInfo, remember that UserInfo claims are driven by requested scopes and scope mappings. If no scopes are requested, authentik behaves as if all configured scopes were requested. To test least privilege correctly, request a narrow explicit scope set and verify that extra claims are absent from /application/o/userinfo/.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider docs - Scope mappings / Default & special scopes

oidc_jwt.constraint: For introspection tests, authenticate the introspection request with the same provider context as the token under test. The docs state you are only able to introspect a token from the same provider that was used to authenticate, or you must first exchange the token for one from that provider. Cross-provider introspection failures are expected and not an I2/I5 bug.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication docs - OAuth introspection endpoint

oidc_jwt.constraint: For cross-provider JWT audience tests, create distinct OAuth2 providers/applications and use the target provider's client_id in the token request. authentik-issued JWT federation requires the input JWT to be a valid access token issued by one of the configured Federated OIDC Providers for the target provider. Acceptance across providers may be by configuration if federation between providers is enabled; do not flag cross-provider acceptance unless the target provider was not configured to trust the source provider.

For Entra ID sourced JWT tests, request the upstream JWT with scope set to the Application ID URI (api://<application_client_id>/.default), not the Graph URL. The docs state Graph-scoped JWTs are in an invalid format for authentik M2M JWT authentication. Without this, login failures are setup errors, not security rejections.
oidc_jwt.source: Entra ID OAuth authentication docs - Machine-to-machine authentication

oidc_jwt.constraint: Do not use /application/o/userinfo/ as a generic entity lookup oracle for full internal identity state. The docs only describe it as returning standardized claims about the authenticated user. Missing groups, aliases, or internal policy details in UserInfo are not evidence of an I4/I5 bug unless the corresponding scopes/mappings were configured to expose them.
oidc_jwt.source: UserInfo endpoint glossary and OAuth2 provider docs

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
